nodes.label: Parent-child hierarchy (RT parent app, Mirage optional capability)
nodes.rationale: RT owns navigation, library, sessions, analytics, goals, and existing persistence; Mirage owns ledger, claims, projection and spoiler policy; neither side may silently become the other's source of truth, and a green suite for either alone proves nothing about the integrated product.
nodes.norm_label: parent-child hierarchy (rt parent app, mirage optional capability)

nodes.label: Explicit non-goals (no store unification, no repo deletion, no auto-analysis)
nodes.rationale: Merge does not mean maximal file movement; stripping these non-goals would couple ownership domains, so only countersigned ADRs may deviate.
nodes.norm_label: explicit non-goals (no store unification, no repo deletion, no auto-analysis)

nodes.label: Identity mapping is a first-class subsystem (no title guessing)
nodes.rationale: Similar concepts do not prove equivalent semantics; a wrong link contaminates analysis, confuses editions, and applies the wrong spoiler cursor, so mapping must be explicit, evidence-classed, and user-confimed when ambiguous.
nodes.norm_label: identity mapping is a first-class subsystem (no title guessing)

nodes.label: Spoiler-cursor boundary (highest-risk semantic boundary)
nodes.rationale: RT counts pages while Mirage counts paragraph units; no verified mapping exists, and it must never guess a later cursor for UI convenience - a missing cursor is not permission to show the whole book.

nodes.label: S10-ES-1 explicit-gesture pre-flight doctrine
nodes.rationale: Imports must record the user gesture, verify sandbox file access and stable stat before dispatch, disclose what will be created in the ledger, and keep cancel live until Mirage's committed point; post-commit is new-state disclosure, never a rollback claim.

nodes.label: S16-ES-1 PR gate ladder (per-PR acceptance gates)

nodes.norm_label: s16-es-1 pr gate ladder (per-pr acceptance gates)

nodes.label: S8-ES-5 house suite standard
nodes.rationale: Gate evidence must meet the recorded house test standard; selectively-passing batch runs do not equivalently satisfy full-runner requirements.

nodes.label: §21 impossibility rule + W3 (no invented wire fields / no ID synthesis)
nodes.rationale: Protocol shapes may only expand via amendment or ADR; RT must never invent Mirage identifiers, because a fabricated ID could silently misdirect analysis into another edition.

nodes.author: Johan Rembeci

nodes.label: Managed stdio NDJSON sidecar transport decision
nodes.rationale: Strongest isolation and parity with the engine's proven surfaces; in-process Python embedding was rejected (RSS budget in the wrong process, runloop coupling, repeat of the MainActor freeze class) and HTTP loopback was rejected as a feature-negative from a sandboxed app.
nodes.norm_label: managed stdio ndjson sidecar transport decision

nodes.label: Operational handshake (health banner → version → api_version pin)
nodes.rationale: No version field exists on the wire, so pinning is operational: spawn-time health banner with status ready plus a version exchange requiring api_version 1.0.0, contract-hash recorded for exactly-match comparison.
nodes.norm_label: operational handshake (health banner → version → api_version pin)

nodes.label: mirageProtocolIncompatible mask (feature masked to status row)
nodes.norm_label: mirageprotocolincompatible mask (feature masked to status row)

nodes.label: Single-instance supervision + bounded restart (≤3 attempts, 2/4/8 s backoff)
nodes.rationale: The supervisor owns exactly one sidecar per ledger (PID-file + liveness at acquire); restarts are bounded so a crashing child can never loop the host, and teardown escalates SIGTERM → 5 s wait → SIGKILL.
nodes.norm_label: single-instance supervision + bounded restart (≤3 attempts, 2/4/8 s backoff)

nodes.label: S2-ES-4 wire discipline (one compact JSON per LF line, no invented fields)
nodes.rationale: UTF-8 no-BOM framing with flush-per-line, id echoed for correlation, and the wire never widened - any future field is a PR-2 amendment or a new ADR.
nodes.norm_label: s2-es-4 wire discipline (one compact json per lf line, no invented fields)

nodes.label: S12-ES-3: localhost is not a trusted call (HTTP disabled inside RT)
nodes.rationale: A local-only service is not automatically safe (DNS rebinding, port conflicts, request-validation divergence), so RT never starts the HTTP surface or web UI and exposes no setting to enable them.
nodes.norm_label: s12-es-3: localhost is not a trusted call (http disabled inside rt)

nodes.label: Pipe I/O on nonisolated worker (no MainActor-blocked work ≥5 ms)
nodes.rationale: All framing and parsing run on a dedicated nonisolated worker so transport work can never freeze the MainActor-default app; handback to MainActor only for UI state mutations.
nodes.norm_label: pipe i/o on nonisolated worker (no mainactor-blocked work ≥5 ms)

nodes.label: Ledger backup ownership = Mirage's own doctrine (RT never fabricates ledger backups)
nodes.rationale: Backing up a large WAL database mid-session from outside the owner process is consistency-hostile; the engine's close-side wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) leaves a self-consistent set, so analysis remains append-only value while RT backups exclude mirage/.

nodes.label: Disable-deletes-nothing doctrine
nodes.rationale: The identity stratum, ledgers, and stored analyses stay byte-identical across enable/disable cycles; destructive ops need their own Class Δ countersigned decision rather than hiding behind a settings toggle.

nodes.label: Independence-by-construction argument (no addBook, no goal machinery)

nodes.label: Structural census gate (zero banned symbols in Mirage feature files)
